Class TypeKey

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.processing.TypeKey
public final class TypeKey extends Object
A TypeMirror with the equals and hashCode of the type it denotes, for use in sets and maps: TypeMirror itself does not define them, and two mirrors of List<String> need not be equal.

Two keys are equal when their types are the same type, as ProcessingContext.isSameType(TypeMirror, TypeMirror) says, ignoring annotations on types at any depth: List<@Nullable String> has the key of List<String>. That is, when their types have the same kind and:

  • for declared types, the same class or interface, equal type arguments and equal enclosing types: Outer<String>.Inner is not Outer<Integer>.Inner, and a raw type is neither a parameterization of its class nor the type of its declaration, List<E>;
  • for arrays, equal components;
  • for type variables, the same type parameter of the same class, method or constructor;
  • for wildcards, equal bounds, an unbounded wildcard being bounded by Object, as javac compares type arguments: ? is ? extends Object, but not ? super Object;
  • for intersection types, equal bounds, in any order;
  • for executable types, equal type variables, parameter types and return type, ignoring thrown types;
  • for primitive types, void and the other kinds of types, nothing more.

As equals must, keys are equal by an equivalence relation, and they need no javac to compare, so they differ from isSameType for these types:

  • a type javac could not resolve, of kind TypeKind.ERROR, is the same type as any type for isSameType, which is no equivalence relation. Its key is equal to the key of an unresolved type only, with the same name as written in the source, without its annotations, the same type arguments and the same enclosing type: @Nullable Missing has the key of Missing, but foo.Missing does not. Some JDKs, as JDK 21, keep neither the name nor the type arguments of an unresolved parameterized type, which they give as <any>: Missing<String> then has the key of Other<Integer>;
  • a generic executable type is the same type for isSameType as another one that only names its type variables differently, as the types of <A> void a(A) and <B> void b(B), while their keys compare their type variables as any other and differ;
  • a union type, the type of a multi-catch parameter, is compared by isSameType by the least upper bound of its alternatives, while its key compares its alternatives, in any order.

Classes and interfaces are known by their canonical name, and type variables by their name and that of their class, method or constructor. Those with no canonical name, as local and anonymous classes and the classes nested in them, and the type variables of captured types, are known by their element: compare their keys within a round.
